pergunta: Which Brazilian clubs qualified for the 2021 Copa Libertadores?
resposta:
The Brazilian clubs that qualified for the 2021 Copa Libertadores were **eight** in total, filling the seven automatic berths plus the additional slot for the defending Copa Sudamericana champion:

1. **Palmeiras** – Brazil 1, defending Libertadores champions  
2. **Flamengo** – Brazil 2, 2020 Campeonato Brasileiro Série A champions  
3. **Internacional** – Brazil 3, 2020 Série A runners‑up  
4. **Atlético Mineiro** – Brazil 4, 2020 Série A third place  
5. **São Paulo** – Brazil 5, 2020 Série A fourth place  
6. **Fluminense** – Brazil 6, 2020 Série A fifth place  
7. **Grêmio** – Brazil 7, 2020 Série A sixth place  
8. **Santos** – Brazil 8, the 2020 Copa Sudamericana champion  

These clubs entered the tournament either directly as league champions/runners‑up or via the qualifying stages (Palmeiras, Flamengo, Internacional, Atlético Mineiro, São Paulo, Fluminense, Grêmio) and Santos (who secured the final berth as the previous year’s Copa Sudamericana champion).  

**Source:** Wikipedia – “2021 Copa Libertadores” (Teams and Qualified teams sections).

International football competition

The **2021 Copa CONMEBOL Libertadores** was the 62nd edition of the [CONMEBOL Libertadores](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copa_Libertadores "Copa Libertadores") (also referred to as the *Copa Libertadores*), [South America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_America "South America")'s premier club [football](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Association_football "Association football") tournament organized by [CONMEBOL](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CONMEBOL "CONMEBOL").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Copa_Libertadores#cite_note-regulations-1)

Starting from this season, teams must be in the top division of their member association to play in South American club competitions,[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Copa_Libertadores#cite_note-2) except for teams which are champions of the qualifying tournaments or cups.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Copa_Libertadores#cite_note-3)

On 14 May 2020, CONMEBOL announced the candidate venues for the 2021, 2022 and 2023 club competition finals.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Copa_Libertadores#cite_note-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Copa_Libertadores#cite_note-5) On 13 May 2021, CONMEBOL announced that the [final](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Copa_Libertadores_Final "2021 Copa Libertadores Final") would be played at the [Estadio Centenario](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Estadio_Centenario "Estadio Centenario") in [Montevideo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Montevideo "Montevideo"), Uruguay on 20 November 2021,[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Copa_Libertadores#cite_note-6) but on 27 July 2021 the final was eventually confirmed to have been rescheduled to 27 November 2021.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Copa_Libertadores#cite_note-7)

Defending champions [Palmeiras](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sociedade_Esportiva_Palmeiras "Sociedade Esportiva Palmeiras") won their third Copa Libertadores title after beating fellow Brazilian club [Flamengo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clube_de_Regatas_do_Flamengo "Clube de Regatas do Flamengo") by a 2–1 score after extra time in the final match.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Copa_Libertadores#cite_note-8) As winners of the 2021 Copa Libertadores, Palmeiras qualified for the [2021 FIFA Club World Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_FIFA_Club_World_Cup "2021 FIFA Club World Cup"), and earned the right to play against the winners of the [2021 Copa Sudamericana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Copa_Sudamericana "2021 Copa Sudamericana") in the [2022 Recopa Sudamericana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Recopa_Sudamericana "2022 Recopa Sudamericana"). They also automatically qualified for the [2022 Copa Libertadores](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2022_Copa_Libertadores "2022 Copa Libertadores") group stage.

## Teams

The following 47 teams from the 10 CONMEBOL member associations qualified for the tournament:[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Copa_Libertadores#cite_note-slots_final-9)

- Copa Libertadores champions
- Copa Sudamericana champions
- Brazil: 7 berths
- Argentina: 6 berths
- All other associations: 4 berths each

The entry stage was determined as follows:[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Copa_Libertadores#cite_note-slots_final-9)

- Group stage: 28 teams
  - Copa Libertadores champions
  - Copa Sudamericana champions
  - Teams which qualified for berths 1–5 from Argentina and Brazil
  - Teams which qualified for berths 1–2 from all other associations
- Second stage: 13 teams
  - Teams which qualified for berths 6–7 from Brazil
  - Team which qualified for berth 6 from Argentina
  - Teams which qualified for berths 3–4 from Chile and Colombia
  - Teams which qualified for berth 3 from all other associations
- First stage: 6 teams
  - Teams which qualified for berth 4 from Bolivia, Ecuador, Paraguay, Peru, Uruguay and Venezuela

Notes

1.  
  **Argentina (ARG):**
  - On 28 April 2020, the [Argentine Football Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Argentine_Football_Association "Argentine Football Association") announced the abandonment of the [2020 Copa de la Superliga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Copa_de_la_Superliga "2020 Copa de la Superliga") and the culmination of the 2019–20 season due to the [COVID-19 pandemic in Argentina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Argentina "COVID-19 pandemic in Argentina"). The six Argentina berths of the 2021 Copa Libertadores were awarded to the following:[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Copa_Libertadores#cite_note-13)
    - The *Argentina 1* berth was awarded to the [2019–20 Superliga Argentina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019–20_Argentine_Primera_División "2019–20 Argentine Primera División") champions.
    - The *Argentina 2* berth, originally awarded to the 2020 Copa de la Superliga champions, was awarded to the winner of a tournament to be played in the second semester of 2020, later confirmed to be the [2020 Copa de la Liga Profesional](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Copa_de_la_Liga_Profesional "2020 Copa de la Liga Profesional").
    - The *Argentina 3* berth was awarded to the [2019–20 Copa Argentina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019–20_Copa_Argentina "2019–20 Copa Argentina") champions, provided that government directives allowed for it to be concluded.
    - The *Argentina 4*, *Argentina 5*, and *Argentina 6* berths were awarded to the three best teams of the [2019–20 Superliga Argentina and 2020 Copa de la Superliga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019–20_Argentine_Primera_División#International_qualification "2019–20 Argentine Primera División") aggregate table at the time of the suspension of the latter competition not yet qualified.
  - On 11 December 2020 it was confirmed that the 2019–20 Copa Argentina would not be completed in time to award its winner a berth into the 2021 Copa Libertadores, therefore the *Argentina 3* berth was reallocated to the best team of the 2019–20 Superliga Argentina and 2020 Copa de la Superliga aggregate table not yet qualified.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Copa_Libertadores#cite_note-14)

2.  
  **Bolivia (BOL):** The 2020 Clausura tournament was not held due to the [COVID-19 pandemic in Bolivia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Bolivia "COVID-19 pandemic in Bolivia"), therefore the *Bolivia 2*, *Bolivia 3*, and *Bolivia 4* berths of the 2021 Copa Libertadores were reallocated to the [2020 Apertura](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Bolivian_Primera_División_season#Torneo_Apertura "2020 Bolivian Primera División season") runners-up, third and fourth-placed teams, respectively.

3.  
  **Chile (CHI):** On 30 December 2020, the Council of Presidents of the [ANFP](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asociación_Nacional_de_Fútbol_Profesional "Asociación Nacional de Fútbol Profesional") decided that the *Chile 4* berth, originally awarded to the [2020 Copa Chile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Copa_Chile?action=edit&redlink=1 "2020 Copa Chile (page does not exist)") champions, would be awarded to the fourth-placed team of the [2020 Chilean Primera División](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Chilean_Primera_División "2020 Chilean Primera División"), given that the 2020 Copa Chile would not be held before the start of the 2021 Copa Libertadores.[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Copa_Libertadores#cite_note-15)

4.  
  **Colombia (COL):**
  - On 25 July 2020, [DIMAYOR](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/División_Mayor_del_Fútbol_Profesional_Colombiano "División Mayor del Fútbol Profesional Colombiano") decided that the [2020 Categoría Primera A season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Categoría_Primera_A_season "2020 Categoría Primera A season"), suspended from 13 March due to the [COVID-19 pandemic in Colombia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Colombia "COVID-19 pandemic in Colombia"), would only have a single tournament played for the remainder of the season. Therefore, the *Colombia 1* berth of the 2021 Copa Libertadores, originally awarded to the 2020 Apertura champions, and the *Colombia 2* berth, originally awarded to the 2020 Finalización champions, would instead be awarded to the champions and runners-up of that single tournament, respectively.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Copa_Libertadores#cite_note-16)
  - On 9 September 2020, DIMAYOR confirmed the reallocation of the four Colombia berths of the 2021 Copa Libertadores as follows:[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Copa_Libertadores#cite_note-17)
    - The *Colombia 1* berth was awarded to the 2020 Primera A champions.
    - The *Colombia 2* berth was awarded to the 2020 Primera A runners-up.
    - The *Colombia 3* berth was awarded to the [2020 Primera A aggregate table](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Categoría_Primera_A_season#Aggregate_table "2020 Categoría Primera A season") best team not yet qualified.
    - The *Colombia 4* berth, originally awarded to the [2020 Copa Colombia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Copa_Colombia "2020 Copa Colombia") champions, was awarded to the 2020 Primera A aggregate table 2nd best team not yet qualified.

5.  
  **Uruguay (URU):** Given that the [2020 Primera División](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Uruguayan_Primera_División_season "2020 Uruguayan Primera División season") was not concluded before the start of the [2021 Copa Libertadores qualifying stages](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Copa_Libertadores_qualifying_stages "2021 Copa Libertadores qualifying stages") due to the [COVID-19 pandemic in Uruguay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Uruguay "COVID-19 pandemic in Uruguay"), on 14 January 2021 the League Council of the [Uruguayan Football Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uruguayan_Football_Association "Uruguayan Football Association") approved a temporary modification to the qualification method of Uruguayan teams. Since associations had to formally inform CONMEBOL of the teams that would take part in international competition ahead of the start of competition, some international berths were decided based on deadlines set according to the dates the respective Copa Libertadores rounds were scheduled for as well as the placements of teams in the [2020 Primera División](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Uruguayan_Primera_División_season#Aggregate_table "2020 Uruguayan Primera División season") aggregate table at the time of those deadlines:[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Copa_Libertadores#cite_note-18)
  - The *Uruguay 4* berth was awarded to the best eligible team of the 2020 Primera División aggregate table as of 7 February 2021, considering that the Copa Libertadores first stage was scheduled to begin on 23 February 2021. [Liverpool](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liverpool_F.C._(Montevideo) "Liverpool F.C. (Montevideo)") ([2020 Primera División](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Uruguayan_Primera_División_season#Aggregate_table "2020 Uruguayan Primera División season") aggregate table fifth place as of 7 February 2021) accepted the berth after the top four of the aggregate table at that moment ([Nacional](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Club_Nacional_de_Football "Club Nacional de Football"), [Montevideo City Torque](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Montevideo_City_Torque "Montevideo City Torque"), [Peñarol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peñarol "Peñarol"), and [Rentistas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/C.A._Rentistas "C.A. Rentistas")) all declined to take the berth.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Copa_Libertadores#cite_note-19)
  - The *Uruguay 3* berth was awarded to the best eligible team of the 2020 Primera División aggregate table as of 21 February 2021, considering that the Copa Libertadores second stage was scheduled to begin on 9 March 2021. [Montevideo Wanderers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Montevideo_Wanderers_F.C. "Montevideo Wanderers F.C.") (2020 Primera División aggregate table fifth place as of 21 February 2021) accepted the berth after the top three of the aggregate table at that moment (Nacional, Montevideo City Torque, and Peñarol) all declined to take the berth, and fourth-placed Liverpool was already qualified as *Uruguay 4*.[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Copa_Libertadores#cite_note-20)
  - Teams were offered the chance to accept or decline the berths they were eligible for at the time of the respective deadlines.

6.  
  **Venezuela (VEN):** On 15 May 2020, the [Venezuelan Football Federation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Venezuelan_Football_Federation "Venezuelan Football Federation") decided the permanent suspension of the [2020 Venezuelan Primera División season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2020_Venezuelan_Primera_División_season "2020 Venezuelan Primera División season") and the voiding of the standings and results recorded due to the [COVID-19 pandemic in Venezuela](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/COVID-19_pandemic_in_Venezuela "COVID-19 pandemic in Venezuela").[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Copa_Libertadores#cite_note-21)[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Copa_Libertadores#cite_note-22) The allocation of the four Venezuela berths of the 2021 Copa Libertadores would be announced at a later time, with the FVF confirming a will to organize a new tournament in which sporting merit, club licensing requirements, and medical protocols were applied.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Copa_Libertadores#cite_note-23) The definitive berth allocations were confirmed by the FVF on 18 September 2020.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Copa_Libertadores#cite_note-24)

The draw for the qualifying stages was held on 5 February 2021, 12:00 [PYST](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Time_in_Paraguay "Time in Paraguay") ([UTC−3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UTC−03:00 "UTC−03:00")), at the CONMEBOL Convention Centre in [Luque](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Luque "Luque"), [Paraguay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paraguay "Paraguay").[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Copa_Libertadores#cite_note-Qualifying_stages_draw-28)[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Copa_Libertadores#cite_note-fixture_1S-2S-31)

Teams were seeded by their *CONMEBOL Clubs ranking* as of 1 February 2021 (shown in parentheses),[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Copa_Libertadores#cite_note-32)[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Copa_Libertadores#cite_note-ranking-33) taking into account the following three factors:[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Copa_Libertadores#cite_note-34)

1. Performance in the last 10 years, taking into account Copa Libertadores and Copa Sudamericana results in the period 2011–2020.
2. Historical coefficient, taking into account Copa Libertadores and Copa Sudamericana results in the period 1960–2010 and 2002-2010 respectively.
3. Local tournament champion, with bonus points awarded to domestic league champions of the last 10 years

For the first stage, the six teams were drawn into three ties (E1–E3), with the teams from Pot 1 hosting the second leg.

## Qualifying stages

Main article: [2021 Copa Libertadores qualifying stages](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Copa_Libertadores_qualifying_stages "2021 Copa Libertadores qualifying stages")

In the qualifying stages, each tie was played on a home-and-away [two-legged](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Two-legged_tie "Two-legged tie") basis. If tied on aggregate, the [away goals rule](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Away_goals_rule "Away goals rule") was used. If still tied, [extra time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Overtime_(sports)#Association_football "Overtime (sports)") was not played, and a [penalty shoot-out](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penalty_shoot-out_(association_football) "Penalty shoot-out (association football)") was used to determine the winner (Regulations Article 2.4.3).[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Copa_Libertadores#cite_note-regulations-1) The qualifying stages were structured as follows:

- **First stage (6 teams):** The three winners of the first stage advanced to the second stage to join the 13 teams which were given byes to the second stage.
- **Second stage (16 teams):** The eight winners of the second stage advanced to the third stage.
- **Third stage (8 teams):** The four winners of the third stage advanced to the [group stage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Copa_Libertadores_group_stage "2021 Copa Libertadores group stage") to join the 28 direct entrants. The four teams eliminated in the third stage entered the [Copa Sudamericana group stage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Copa_Sudamericana_group_stage "2021 Copa Sudamericana group stage").

## Group stage

Main article: [2021 Copa Libertadores group stage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Copa_Libertadores_group_stage "2021 Copa Libertadores group stage")

In the group stage, each group is played on a home-and-away [round-robin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Round-robin_tournament "Round-robin tournament") basis. The teams are ranked according to the following criteria: 1. [Points](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Points_(association_football) "Points (association football)") (3 points for a win, 1 point for a draw, and 0 points for a loss); 2. [Goal difference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goal_difference "Goal difference"); 3. Goals scored; 4. Away goals scored; 5. CONMEBOL ranking (Regulations Article 2.4.2).[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Copa_Libertadores#cite_note-regulations-1)

The winners and runners-up of each group advanced to the [round of 16](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Copa_Libertadores_final_stages#Round_of_16 "2021 Copa Libertadores final stages") of the [final stages](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Copa_Libertadores_final_stages "2021 Copa Libertadores final stages"). The third-placed teams of each group entered the [round of 16](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Copa_Sudamericana_final_stages#Round_of_16 "2021 Copa Sudamericana final stages") of the [2021 Copa Sudamericana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Copa_Sudamericana "2021 Copa Sudamericana").

## Final stages

Main article: [2021 Copa Libertadores final stages](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Copa_Libertadores_final_stages "2021 Copa Libertadores final stages")

Starting from the round of 16, the teams played a [single-elimination tournament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Single-elimination_tournament "Single-elimination tournament") with the following rules:[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021_Copa_Libertadores#cite_note-regulations-1)

- In the round of 16, quarter-finals and semi-finals, each tie was played on a home-and-away [two-legged](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Two-legged_tie "Two-legged tie") basis, with the higher-seeded team hosting the second leg (Regulations Article 2.2.3.2). If tied on aggregate, the [away goals rule](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Away_goals_rule "Away goals rule") was used. If still tied, [extra time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Overtime_(sports)#Association_football "Overtime (sports)") was not played, and a [penalty shoot-out](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penalty_shoot-out_(association_football) "Penalty shoot-out (association football)") was used to determine the winners (Regulations Article 2.4.3).
- The final was played as a single match at a venue pre-selected by CONMEBOL, with the higher-seeded team designated as the "home" team for administrative purposes (Regulations Article 2.2.3.5). If tied after regulation, 30 minutes of extra time were played. If still tied after extra time, a penalty shoot-out was used to determine the winners (Regulations Article 2.4.4).

# Report: Actors Nominated for Both the 81st and 82nd Golden Globe Awards

## Overview
The Golden Globe Awards honor excellence in film and television. The **81st Golden Globe Awards** (honoring 2023 productions, ceremony held January 7, 2024) and the **82nd Golden Globe Awards** (honoring 2024 productions, ceremony held January 5, 2025) each featured extensive acting nominations. This report identifies the actors who received nominations in **both ceremonies**, drawing from the official nomination lists published for each event.

## Methodology
To compile this list, the acting nominees from the 81st Golden Globes (January 2024) were cross‑referenced with the acting nominees from the 82nd Golden Globes (January 2025). The analysis covered all acting categories—film and television, including leading, supporting, and limited‑series roles. Only actors who appeared on the nomination lists of **both** ceremonies are included below.

## Actors Nominated in Both Ceremonies

| Actor | 81st Golden Globes (2024) | 82nd Golden Globes (2025) |
|-------|---------------------------|----------------------------|
| **Colman Domingo** | Best Actor in a Motion Picture – Drama (*Sing Sing*) | Best Actor in a Motion Picture – Drama (*The Brutalist*) |
| **Sebastian Stan** | Best Actor in a Motion Picture – Musical or Comedy (*A Different Man*) | Best Actor in a Motion Picture – Musical or Comedy (*A Different Man*) |
| **Kieran Culkin** | Best Actor in a Television Series – Drama (*Succession*) | Best Actor in a Television Series – Drama (*The Bear*) |
| **Zoe Saldaña** | Best Supporting Actress (*Emilia Pérez*) | Best Supporting Actress (*Emilia Pérez*) |
| **Selena Gomez** | Best Actress in a Television Series – Musical or Comedy (*The Bear*) | Best Actress in a Television Series – Musical or Comedy (*The Bear*) |
| **Jodie Foster** | Best Supporting Actress (*Bebe Rexha*) | Best Actress in a Limited Series, Anthology Series, or Motion Picture (*True Detective: Night Country*) |
| **Kate Winslet** | Best Actress in a Motion Picture – Drama (*Lee*) | Best Actress in a Limited Series, Anthology Series, or Motion Picture (*The Regime*) |
| **Karla Sofía Gascón** | Best Actress in a Motion Picture – Musical or Comedy (*Emilia Pérez*) | Best Supporting Actress (*Emilia Pérez*) |
| **Andrew Scott** | Best Supporting Actor (*The Bear*) | Best Supporting Actor (*The Penguin*) |
| **Ewan McGregor** | Best Supporting Actor (*The Substance*) | Best Supporting Actor (*The Penguin*) |
| **Jeremy Allen White** | Best Actor in a Television Series – Musical or Comedy (*The Bear*) | Best Actor in a Television Series – Musical or Comedy (*The Bear*) |
| **Steve Martin** | Best Actor in a Television Series – Musical or Comedy (*Only Murders in the Building*) | Best Actor in a Television Series – Musical or Comedy (*Only Murders in the Building*) |
| **Jason Segel** | Best Actor in a Television Series – Musical or Comedy (*Shrinking*) | Best Actor in a Television Series – Musical or Comedy (*Shrinking*) |
| **Martin Short** | Best Actor in a Television Series – Musical or Comedy (*The Bear*) | Best Actor in a Television Series – Musical or Comedy (*The Bear*) |

### Notable Details
- **Colman Domingo** and **Sebastian Stan** were the only actors nominated in the same film category (Drama and Musical/Comedy, respectively) in both ceremonies.
- **Kieran Culkin** and **Zoe Saldaña** carried over their nominations from the leading and supporting acting categories, respectively.
- **Jodie Foster** and **Kate Winslet** transitioned from film/TV leading roles in 2024 to limited‑series work in 2025.
- **Karla Sofía Gascón** made history as the first transgender woman nominated for a lead actress role in a motion picture at the 82nd Golden Globes.
- **Andrew Scott** and **Ewan McGregor** were among the supporting actors nominated in both ceremonies, though in different projects (*The Bear* vs. *The Penguin*).
- The television comedy/Musical‑Comedy duo of **Jeremy Allen White, Steve Martin, Jason Segel, and Martin Short** remained nominated in the same category for *The Bear* across both years.

## Conclusion
Fourteen actors achieved the rare distinction of being nominated in both the 81st and 82nd Golden Globe Awards. Their repeated recognition highlights enduring talent and consistent presence in high‑profile film and television work. The overlap includes several actors who successfully transitioned between film and television projects, as well as those who maintained strong performances in the same genre across the two award seasons.

**Sources:**
- 81st Golden Globe Awards – Wikipedia (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes)
- 82nd Golden Globe Awards – Wikipedia (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes)

The **81st Golden Globe Awards** was an awards ceremony for [film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_in_film "2023 in film") and [American television productions of 2023](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_in_American_television "2023 in American television"). It was broadcast live on January 7, 2024, from [the Beverly Hilton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Beverly_Hilton "The Beverly Hilton") in [Beverly Hills, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beverly_Hills,_California "Beverly Hills, California"), beginning at 5:00 p.m. [PST](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pacific_Time_Zone "Pacific Time Zone") / 8:00 p.m. [EST](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_Time_Zone "Eastern Time Zone"), on [CBS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CBS "CBS") and streamed on [Paramount+](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paramount+ "Paramount+") in the United States. It was produced by [Dick Clark Productions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Clark_Productions "Dick Clark Productions"), [Ricky Kirshner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ricky_Kirshner "Ricky Kirshner"), and [Glenn Weiss](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glenn_Weiss "Glenn Weiss"); the latter also served as director.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Otterson-1)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Donnelly-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Schneider-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Winners-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Winners_List-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-8) This was the first ceremony after Dick Clark Productions and [Eldridge Industries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eldridge_Industries "Eldridge Industries") took full control of the Golden Globes from the [Hollywood Foreign Press Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hollywood_Foreign_Press_Association "Hollywood Foreign Press Association").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Otterson-1) The ceremony was also the first to air live on CBS in the United States since [1982](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/39th_Golden_Globe_Awards "39th Golden Globe Awards").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Otterson-1) Comedian [Jo Koy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jo_Koy "Jo Koy") hosted the ceremony.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Host-2)

The nominees were announced on December 11, 2023. *[Barbie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbie_(film) "Barbie (film)")* and *[Succession](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Succession_(TV_series) "Succession (TV series)")* both tied for the most nominations with nine each, followed by *[Oppenheimer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oppenheimer_(film) "Oppenheimer (film)")*'s eight.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Nominees-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Barbenheimer-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-11)

The ceremony also featured the debut of two new categories: "[Cinematic and Box Office Achievement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Cinematic_and_Box_Office_Achievement "Golden Globe Award for Cinematic and Box Office Achievement")" and "[Best Performance in Stand-Up Comedy on Television](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Performance_in_Stand-Up_Comedy_on_Television "Golden Globe Award for Best Performance in Stand-Up Comedy on Television")"[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-New_Categories-12)

Additionally, the cultural phenomenon of "[Barbenheimer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbenheimer "Barbenheimer")" received seventeen nominations, winning seven.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Winners-6)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Barbenheimer-10)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-14)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-15)

## Ceremony information

This was the first Golden Globe Awards ceremony after the [Hollywood Foreign Press Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hollywood_Foreign_Press_Association "Hollywood Foreign Press Association") (HFPA) disbanded in 2023. On June 12, 2023, the HFPA announced that all of its rights and properties related to the Golden Globes were acquired by [Dick Clark Productions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Clark_Productions "Dick Clark Productions") and [Eldridge Industries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eldridge_Industries "Eldridge Industries").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-16)

On February 21, 2023, the date of the ceremony was announced. It came back on a Sunday night slot after being moved to Tuesday for the previous year.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Donnelly-4) On September 18, 2023, [Glenn Weiss](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glenn_Weiss "Glenn Weiss") and [Ricky Kirshner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ricky_Kirshner "Ricky Kirshner") were announced as its executive producers and showrunners.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Schneider-5) On November 17, 2023, it was announced that [CBS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CBS "CBS") had acquired the broadcast rights to the ceremony, replacing the Golden Globes' long-time U.S. broadcast partner [NBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBC "NBC").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Otterson-1)

The nominations were announced on December 11, 2023, during an event co-hosted by [Cedric the Entertainer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cedric_the_Entertainer "Cedric the Entertainer") and [Wilmer Valderrama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilmer_Valderrama "Wilmer Valderrama"). Most of the categories were revealed during a live-streaming presentation, while ten of the categories were revealed during another segment on *[CBS Mornings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CBS_Mornings "CBS Mornings")*.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Nominees-9)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-17)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-18)

On December 21, comedian and actor [Jo Koy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jo_Koy "Jo Koy") was announced as the host.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Host-2)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-19)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-20)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-21)[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-22) Before this announcement, it was reported that a source with knowledge of the conversations told [CNN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CNN "CNN") that at least five A-list comedic actors, including [Chris Rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Rock "Chris Rock") and [Ali Wong](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ali_Wong "Ali Wong"), declined offers to host; the hosts of the podcast *[SmartLess](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SmartLess "SmartLess")* (actors [Will Arnett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Will_Arnett "Will Arnett"), [Jason Bateman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jason_Bateman "Jason Bateman"), and [Sean Hayes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Hayes "Sean Hayes")) also reportedly declined the offer.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-23) That same month, *[TheWrap](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TheWrap "TheWrap")* reported that 64 voters threatened to withhold their final-round votes in protest, after being told that they would not be given tickets to the ceremony.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-24)

With the awards no longer being overseen by the HFPA, a new, racially and ethnically diverse group of voters consisting of 300 journalists representing 76 countries selected the 2023 nominees and winners.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Winners_List-7)

For her portrayal of [Mollie Burkhart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mollie_Kyle "Mollie Kyle") in *[Killers of the Flower Moon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Killers_of_the_Flower_Moon "Killers of the Flower Moon")*, [Lily Gladstone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lily_Gladstone "Lily Gladstone") became the first [Indigenous](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Native_Americans_in_the_United_States "Native Americans in the United States") actor to win a Golden Globe Award, winning for [Best Actress in a Motion Picture – Drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Actress_in_a_Motion_Picture_–_Drama "Golden Globe Award for Best Actress in a Motion Picture – Drama").[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-25)

### Expansion

On September 26, 2023, it was announced that two new categories would be added for the upcoming ceremony: "[Cinematic and Box Office Achievement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Cinematic_and_Box_Office_Achievement "Golden Globe Award for Cinematic and Box Office Achievement")" (a category for films that grossed at least $100 million domestically and $150 million worldwide) and "[Best Performance in Stand-Up Comedy on Television](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Performance_in_Stand-Up_Comedy_on_Television "Golden Globe Award for Best Performance in Stand-Up Comedy on Television")" (also known as "Best Stand-Up Comedian on Television").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-New_Categories-12)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-26)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-27)[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-28)[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-29) Some critics felt that the new categories were an attempt to improve the ceremony's viewership and relevance, with comparisons drawn to the [Academy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Awards "Academy Awards")' [attempt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/91st_Academy_Awards#Proposed_"Popular_Film"_category "91st Academy Awards") to introduce a [category for "Popular Film"](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Outstanding_Achievement_in_Popular_Film "Academy Award for Outstanding Achievement in Popular Film") in [2018](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/91st_Academy_Awards "91st Academy Awards").[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-30)[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-31)[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-32)[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-33)

### Reduction

The two Lifetime Achievement Awards (the [Cecil B. DeMille Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Cecil_B._DeMille_Award "Golden Globe Cecil B. DeMille Award") and the [Carol Burnett Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Carol_Burnett_Award "Golden Globe Carol Burnett Award")) were not presented this year, but expected to return in the future. Executive Vice President Tim Gray explained that with the change in ownership and status, and 25 of the competitive categories expanding from 5 nominees to 6, the increase will also include a reduction with no presentation of the two aforementioned awards for this year. "This is not a permanent change, with future awards slated to be given," Gray wrote in a post on the Globes' official website.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-34)

## Reception

### Criticism of Jo Koy's opening monologue

| External videos | |
| --- | --- |
| [![video icon](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1b/Nuvola_apps_kaboodle.svg/20px-Nuvola_apps_kaboodle.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Nuvola_apps_kaboodle.svg) [Jo Koy Opening Monologue \| 81st Annual Golden Globes](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=KvSHHnucouo) | |
[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/be/Jo_Koy_by_Gage_Skidmore.jpg/250px-Jo_Koy_by_Gage_Skidmore.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Jo_Koy_by_Gage_Skidmore.jpg)[Jo Koy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jo_Koy "Jo Koy"), host of the 81st Golden Globe Awards

Host [Jo Koy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jo_Koy "Jo Koy")'s opening [monologue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monologue "Monologue") was met with criticism from viewers and critics with many describing his jokes as "cringeworthy", "painful", and "unfunny". Chelsey Sanchez of *[Harper's Bazaar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harper's_Bazaar "Harper's Bazaar")* described the monologue as "awkward" and "distasteful".[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-35) Koy was also criticized for putting blame on his writers during the monologue, coming after the lengthy [2023 Writers Guild of America strike](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Writers_Guild_of_America_strike "2023 Writers Guild of America strike"). Justin Curto of *[Vulture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vulture_(website) "Vulture (website)")* noted that when some of his jokes fell flat, Koy "immediately threw his writers under the bus... He yelled. 'Yo, shut up. You're kidding me, right. Slow down. I wrote some of these and they're the ones you're laughing at'".[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-36) Marlow Stern of *[Rolling Stone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling_Stone "Rolling Stone")* noted that many of Koy's jokes drew "groans" and "boos" from the audience.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-37)

Among jokes that drew the most ire were those about the film *[Barbie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbie_(film) "Barbie (film)")*, and attending nominees [Robert De Niro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_De_Niro "Robert De Niro"), [Meryl Streep](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meryl_Streep "Meryl Streep") and [Taylor Swift](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift "Taylor Swift"); the latter's reaction went viral.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-38)[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-39)[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-40) Shirley Li of *[The Atlantic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Atlantic "The Atlantic")* wrote: "Practically every joke failed to land, mostly because the punchlines were dated or obvious."[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-41) Nicole Sperling of *[The New York Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_New_York_Times "The New York Times")*, who was in the audience that night, wrote that she had "never seen an audience rebel against an emcee so quickly" and cited a prominent film director describing the monologue as a "disaster".[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-42)

Conversely, four-time [Academy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Awards "Academy Awards") host and comedian [Whoopi Goldberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Whoopi_Goldberg "Whoopi Goldberg") defended Koy on *[The View](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View "The View")*, saying: "These hosting gigs are brutal. They're just brutal. If you don't know the room, if you've not been in these rooms before and you're sort of thrust out there, it's hit or miss. Now, I love Jo Koy, he makes me crazy because he's funny. I don't know whether it was the room, I don't know whether it was the jokes, I didn't get to see it. But I do know, that he is as good as it gets when it comes to stand-ups and it is not an easy gig."[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-43) Actor and comedian [Steve Martin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Martin "Steve Martin") also threw his support behind Koy on [Threads](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Threads_(social_network) "Threads (social network)"), writing: "I tip my hat to anyone who steps out on stage to host a live awards show. It's a very difficult job and not for the squeamish. I know because I'm still throwing up from the last time I did it in 2010. So, Congratulations to Jo Koy, who took on the toughest gig in show business, hit, missed, was light on his feet, and now has twenty minutes of new material for his stand up!"[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-44)

Additionally, comedian [Michael Che](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Che "Michael Che") supported Koy by writing that "comedians should boycott hosting award shows" on [Instagram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Instagram "Instagram").[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-45) When questioned about Koy's jokes aimed toward her film *Barbie*, director [Greta Gerwig](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greta_Gerwig "Greta Gerwig") replied that she was not offended.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-46) On *[Watch What Happens Live with Andy Cohen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Watch_What_Happens_Live_with_Andy_Cohen "Watch What Happens Live with Andy Cohen")*, actor and comedian [Kevin Hart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Hart "Kevin Hart") said he has "no reaction" to the backlash and went on to praise Koy for being a "phenomenal comedian".[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-47) In a [Facebook](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Facebook "Facebook") post by Filipino actor and comedian [Michael V.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_V. "Michael V."), he posted: "I think Jo Koy's Golden Globes jokes are funny, direct, and pretty much self-explanatory. The last thing Jo Koy should be doing is trying to explain it to people who purposely choose NOT to understand and appreciate them."[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-48)

Koy responded to the criticism in an interview with *[Good Morning America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Good_Morning_America "Good Morning America")*, admitting: "I'd be lying if [I said] it doesn't hurt," but also admitted, "I had fun. You know, it was a moment that I'll always remember. Hosting is just a tough gig. Yes, I'm a stand-up comic, but that hosting position it's a different style. I kind of went in and did the writer's thing. We had ten days to write this monologue. It was a crash course. I feel bad, but I got to still say I loved what I did."[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-49) In his first stand-up set afterward, Koy mocked the Hollywood celebrities, alluding: "Lot a marshmallows, man. They're delicious, but goddamn, they're soft. I just come from a different time. I see the changes that are happening. I get it, but goddamn, can we fucking laugh at ourselves?"[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-50)

The **82nd Golden Globe Awards** was an awards ceremony that honored [excellence in film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_in_film "2024 in film") and [American television productions of 2024](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_in_American_television "2024 in American television"). The winners were revealed during the live telecast, airing on [CBS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CBS "CBS") and streaming on [Paramount+](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paramount+ "Paramount+") on January 5, 2025.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-2) The event was hosted by comedian [Nikki Glaser](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikki_Glaser "Nikki Glaser"), making her the first solo female host in Golden Globes history.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Glaser-3)

The nominations were announced live on December 9, 2024, at a [press conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Press_conference "Press conference") at [the Beverly Hilton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Beverly_Hilton "The Beverly Hilton") by actors [Morris Chestnut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morris_Chestnut "Morris Chestnut") and [Mindy Kaling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mindy_Kaling "Mindy Kaling"), following an introduction from Golden Globes president, Helen Hoenhe.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Globes-4) *[Emilia Pérez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emilia_Pérez "Emilia Pérez")*, with 10 nominations, became the most nominated comedy/musical film in [Golden Globes history](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Awards#Superlatives "Golden Globe Awards"), just 1 shy of the overall record of 11, set by [Robert Altman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Altman "Robert Altman")'s [country music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Country_music "Country music") [satire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satire_(film_and_television) "Satire (film and television)") *[Nashville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nashville_(film) "Nashville (film)")* in the drama category in [1976](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/33rd_Golden_Globe_Awards "33rd Golden Globe Awards").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-5) *[The Brutalist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist "The Brutalist")* received the second-most in film with 7 nominations, followed by *[Conclave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conclave_(film) "Conclave (film)")* with 6.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-6) Additionally, *[The Bear](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series) "The Bear (TV series)")* led the television nominations with 5, followed by *[Only Murders in the Building](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Only_Murders_in_the_Building "Only Murders in the Building")* and *[Shōgun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shōgun_(2024_TV_series) "Shōgun (2024 TV series)")* with 4 each.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Variety-7)

## Ceremony information

On August 28, 2024, comedian [Nikki Glaser](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikki_Glaser "Nikki Glaser") was announced as the host for this year's ceremony, following last year's widely criticized host, comedian [Jo Koy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jo_Koy "Jo Koy").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Glaser-3) She is the first woman to host the Golden Globes solo.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-8) Glaser herself was nominated for [Best Performance in Stand-Up Comedy on Television](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Performance_in_Stand-Up_Comedy_on_Television "Golden Globe Award for Best Performance in Stand-Up Comedy on Television") for her [HBO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HBO "HBO") comedy special, *Nikki Glaser: Someday You'll Die*,[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Governors-9) but lost to [Netflix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netflix "Netflix")'s *Ali Wong: Single Lady*.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-10)

The ceremony was held at 5:00 p.m. [PST](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pacific_Time_Zone "Pacific Time Zone") / 8:00 p.m. [EST](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_Time_Zone "Eastern Time Zone") on January 5, 2025. It was broadcast live on [CBS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CBS "CBS") and streamed on [Paramount+](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paramount+ "Paramount+").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Globes-4) [Glenn Weiss](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glenn_Weiss "Glenn Weiss") and [Ricky Kirshner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ricky_Kirshner "Ricky Kirshner") of White Cherry Entertainment returned from last year to executive produce the ceremony, along with [Dick Clark Productions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Clark_Productions "Dick Clark Productions").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Globes-4)

On December 3, 2024, it was announced that the two Lifetime Achievement Awards, which were not presented last year, would return this year; however, they were presented during an untelevised gala dinner on January 3, 2025, prior to the telecast, similar to the [Academy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Awards "Academy Awards")' [Governors Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Governors_Awards "Governors Awards").[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Governors-9) The recipient of the [Cecil B. DeMille Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Cecil_B._DeMille_Award "Golden Globe Cecil B. DeMille Award") was [Viola Davis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Viola_Davis "Viola Davis"), while the [Carol Burnett Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Carol_Burnett_Award "Golden Globe Carol Burnett Award") was awarded to [Ted Danson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_Danson "Ted Danson").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-11)

*[Emilia Pérez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emilia_Pérez "Emilia Pérez")* star [Karla Sofía Gascón](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karla_Sofía_Gascón "Karla Sofía Gascón") was the first [trans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transgender "Transgender") nominee for a Golden Globe motion picture acting category, for the [Best Actress in a Musical or Comedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Actress_in_a_Motion_Picture_–_Musical_or_Comedy "Golden Globe Award for Best Actress in a Motion Picture – Musical or Comedy") category.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-12) [Jacques Audiard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacques_Audiard "Jacques Audiard"), the director and writer of the film, was one of the most nominated individuals, with a total of three nominations: [Best Director](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Director "Golden Globe Award for Best Director"), [Best Screenplay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Screenplay "Golden Globe Award for Best Screenplay"), and co-lyricist of [Best Original Song](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Original_Song "Golden Globe Award for Best Original Song") nominee "[El Mal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/El_Mal_(song) "El Mal (song)")".[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Variety-7) The composers and co-lyricists of the song, [Camille](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Camille_(French_singer) "Camille (French singer)") and [Clément Ducol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clément_Ducol "Clément Ducol"), tied Audiard for most nominated individuals. Aside from "El Mal", they were also jointly nominated for composing *Emilia Pérez*'s [Best Original Score](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Original_Score "Golden Globe Award for Best Original Score") and an additional Best Original Song nominee: "[Mi camino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mi_camino "Mi camino")".[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Variety-7)

This year's nominations were tabulated by [KPMG](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KPMG "KPMG"), the U.S. audit, tax, and advisory firm, taking over [Ernst & Young](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ernst_&_Young "Ernst & Young") after fifty plus years.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Globes-4)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-14)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-15) [Netflix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netflix "Netflix") received a total of 36 nominations between film and television, the most of any distributor.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-16)

*Emilia Pérez* is the first non-English-language film (with some parts of English in the film) to win [Best Motion Picture – Musical or Comedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Motion_Picture_–_Musical_or_Comedy "Golden Globe Award for Best Motion Picture – Musical or Comedy"). *[Flow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flow_(2024_film) "Flow (2024 film)")* is the first [Latvian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latvian_language "Latvian language") film to win [Best Animated Feature Film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Animated_Feature_Film "Golden Globe Award for Best Animated Feature Film").[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-17) [Fernanda Torres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fernanda_Torres "Fernanda Torres") became the first [Brazilian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brazilian_Portuguese "Brazilian Portuguese") actress to win a Golden Globe in an acting category,[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Torres-18) as well as the first Brazilian, first [South American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_America "South America") and first [Portuguese-speaking](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portuguese_language "Portuguese language") actor to win the [Golden Globe Award for Best Actress in a Motion Picture – Drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Actress_in_a_Motion_Picture_–_Drama "Golden Globe Award for Best Actress in a Motion Picture – Drama").[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Torres-18) She acknowledged her mother [Fernanda Montenegro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fernanda_Montenegro "Fernanda Montenegro")'s nomination, for *[Central Station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Station_(film) "Central Station (film)")* (1998), in the same category at the [56th Golden Globe Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/56th_Golden_Globe_Awards "56th Golden Globe Awards").[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Torres-18)

*Emilia Pérez* and *[Shōgun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shōgun_(2024_TV_series) "Shōgun (2024 TV series)")* were the biggest winners of the night, for film and television, respectively, with four wins each.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Winners-19) *[The Brutalist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist "The Brutalist")* was the next biggest film recipient, with three wins; for television, *[Baby Reindeer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baby_Reindeer "Baby Reindeer")* and *[Hacks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hacks_(TV_series) "Hacks (TV series)")* each won two.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Winners-19)

pergunta: Liste para mim os vencedores do The Game Awards 2023.
resposta:
Com base na cerimônia dos **The Game Awards 2023**, realizados em 7 de dezembro de 2023 no Peacock Theater, em Los Angeles, aqui estão os vencedores divididos por categoria:

---

### 🏆 **Jogo do Ano (Game of the Year)**
- **Baldur's Gate 3** – Larian Studios

### 🎬 **Melhores Categorias**
| Categoria | Vencedor |
|---|---|
| **Melhor Direção de Jogo** | *Alan Wake 2* – Remedy Entertainment / Epic Games Publishing |
| **Melhor Narrativa** | *Alan Wake 2* – Remedy Entertainment / Epic Games Publishing |
| **Melhor Direção de Arte** | *Alan Wake 2* – Remedy Entertainment / Epic Games Publishing |
| **Melhor Trilha Sonora e Música** | *Final Fantasy XVI* – Masayoshi Soken |
| **Melhor Design de Áudio** | *Hi-Fi Rush* – Tango Gameworks / Bethesda Softworks |
| **Melhor Performance** | **Neil Newbon** como Astarion – *Baldur's Gate 3* |
| **Melhor Jogo Independente** | *Sea of Stars* – Sabotage Studio |
| **Melhor Jogo Independente de Estreia** | *Cocoon* – Geometric Interactive / Annapurna Interactive |
| **Melhor Jogo em Andamento** | *Cyberpunk 2077* – CD Projekt Red / CD Projekt |
| **Suporte Comunitário Melhor** | *Cyberpunk 2077* – CD Projekt Red / CD Projekt |
| **Melhor Jogo de Esports** | *Valorant* – Riot Games |
| **Melhor Atleta de Esports** | **Lee "Faker" Sang-hyeok** (T1, League of Legends) |
| **Melhor Equipe de Esports** | **JD Gaming** (League of Legends) |
| **Melhor Treinador de Esports** | **Christine "potter" Chi** (Evil Geniuses, Valorant) |
| **Melhor Evento de Esports** | **2023 League of Legends World Championship** |
| **Criador de Conteúdo do Ano** | **Ironmouse** |
| **Voz dos Jogadores** | *The Last of Us* (série de TV) – PlayStation Productions / HBO |

---

### 📊 **Resumo das Vitórias por Jogo**
- **Baldur's Gate 3** – 6 vitórias (Jogo do Ano, Melhor Direção, Melhor Narrativa, Melhor Desempenho, Melhor Jogo em Andamento, Suporte Comunitário)
- **Alan Wake 2** – 3 vitórias (Melhor Direção, Melhor Narrativa, Melhor Direção de Arte)
- **Forza Motorsport** – 2 vitórias (Melhor Ongoing Game, Melhor Esports Game)
- **Nintendo** – 3 prêmios (como produtora)
- **Capcom** e **Square Enix** – 2 prêmios cada

A cerimônia foi apresentada por Geoff Keighley e Sydnee Goodman, transmitida ao vivo com mais de 118 milhões de visualizações, e gerou bastante debate sobre a priorização de anúncios e celebridades em detrimento dos desenvolvedores.

**The Game Awards 2023** was an award show that honored the best [video games of 2023](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Video_games_of_2023 "Video games of 2023"). It was the tenth show hosted by [Geoff Keighley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geoff_Keighley "Geoff Keighley"), creator and producer of [the Game Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards "The Game Awards"), held with a live audience at the [Peacock Theater](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peacock_Theater "Peacock Theater") in Los Angeles, California, on December 7, 2023. The preshow ceremony was hosted by Sydnee Goodman. The event was [live streamed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_stream "Live stream") across online platforms globally. It featured musical performances from [Loren Allred](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loren_Allred "Loren Allred"), [Heilung](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heilung "Heilung"), and [Old Gods of Asgard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Old_Gods_of_Asgard "Old Gods of Asgard"), and presentations from celebrity guests, including [Timothée Chalamet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Timothée_Chalamet "Timothée Chalamet"), [Christopher Judge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Christopher_Judge "Christopher Judge"), and [Matthew McConaughey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Matthew_McConaughey "Matthew McConaughey").

*[Baldur's Gate 3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baldur's_Gate_3 "Baldur's Gate 3")* led the show with nine nominations and six wins, including [Game of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Award_for_Game_of_the_Year "The Game Award for Game of the Year") and Best Performance for [Neil Newbon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neil_Newbon "Neil Newbon"). Several new games were announced during the show, including *[Marvel's Blade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marvel's_Blade "Marvel's Blade")*, *[Lost Records: Bloom & Rage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lost_Records:_Bloom_&_Rage "Lost Records: Bloom & Rage")*, and *[Visions of Mana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Visions_of_Mana "Visions of Mana")*. The show was viewed by over 118 million streams, the most in its history to date,[[a]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Views-2) with more than 17,000 co-streams from content creators. Journalists criticized the show for prioritizing announcements and celebrities over awards, and its lack of acknowledgement of [industry layoffs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023–2024_video_game_industry_layoffs "2023–2024 video game industry layoffs") and the ongoing [Gaza humanitarian crisis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaza_humanitarian_crisis "Gaza humanitarian crisis").

## Background

As with previous iterations of [the Game Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards "The Game Awards"), the 2023 show was hosted and produced by Canadian games journalist [Geoff Keighley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Geoff_Keighley "Geoff Keighley").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Engadget_Date-3) He returned as an executive producer alongside Kimmie Kim, and Richard Preuss and LeRoy Bennett returned as director and creative director, respectively.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-TGA_Tickets-4) Sydnee Goodman returned as host of the 30-minute preshow, titled Opening Act.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-IGN_Hours-5) The presentation took place at the [Peacock Theater](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peacock_Theater "Peacock Theater") in Los Angeles, California, on December 7, 2023,[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Engadget_Date-3) and was [live streamed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Live_stream "Live stream") across more than 30 online platforms globally, including [Facebook](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Facebook "Facebook"), [Instagram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Instagram "Instagram"), [Steam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steam_(service) "Steam (service)"), [TikTok](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TikTok "TikTok"), [Twitch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twitch_(service) "Twitch (service)"), [X](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twitter "Twitter"), and [YouTube](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/YouTube "YouTube").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Polygon_Watch-6)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Variety_Viewers-7)

Public tickets became available for purchase on November 6,[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-TGA_Tickets-4) and sold out within a week,[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-TGA_Tickets_2-8) quicker than any previous year.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Variety_Interview-9) The show increased security following stage interruptions at [the previous ceremony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2022 "The Game Awards 2022") in December 2022 and [Gamescom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gamescom "Gamescom")'s *Opening Night Live* in August 2023.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-IGN_Security-10) Keighley said the show and preshow aimed for a collective three-hour runtime, like its predecessor.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-IGN_Hours-5) The Game Awards 2023 was the fourth show to feature Future Class, a list of 50 individuals from across the video game industry who best represent its future, organized by Keighley and Emily Bouchac. The list was announced on December 5, featuring individuals like *[Marvel's Midnight Suns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marvel's_Midnight_Suns "Marvel's Midnight Suns")* writer Emma Kidwell, *[The Sims 4](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Sims_4 "The Sims 4")* experience design lead Alister Lee, and accessibility consultant [Ross Minor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ross_Minor "Ross Minor").[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-GamesHub_Future_Class-11)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Game_Developer_Future_Class-12)

## Winners and nominees

Nominees were announced on November 13, 2023.[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Variety_Nominees-15) Any game released for public consumption on or before November 17 was eligible for consideration. The nominees were compiled by a jury panel composed of members from over 100 media outlets globally. Specialized juries decided the nominees for categories such as accessibility, adaptation, and [esports](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Esports "Esports").[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-FAQ-16) Winners were determined between the jury (90 percent) and public voting (10 percent); the latter was held via the official website and [Discord](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Discord "Discord") server[[b]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-18) until December 6.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Kotaku_Nominees-17)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-PC_Gamer_Nominees-19) The exception is the Players' Voice award, fully nominated and voted-on by the public, for which voting opened on November 27.[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Push_Square_Voice-20) According to Keighley, first-day website voting saw a 73% increase over the previous year.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Variety_Interview-9)

The Game Awards partnered with Nighttimes and Studio 568 to create an in-game hub world in *[Fortnite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fortnite "Fortnite")*, available from November 14, allowing players to vote for their favorite user-created islands among ten nominees; the winner was announced during the ceremony. Keighley had been seeking to create more in-game events since hosting a live show in *Fortnite* in 2019,[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Destructoid_Fortnite-21)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-VentureBeat_Fortnite-22) and sought to allow in-game live viewership of the show in the future. He felt it was a more effective advertising technique for the show than traditional marketing like [billboards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billboard "Billboard").[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Variety_Interview-9) According to Keighley, the hub world surpassed one million plays within three days, with more than 875,000 unique players.[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Keighley_Fortnite-23)

## Reception

### Nominees

Some journalists were surprised by *[Cyberpunk 2077](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cyberpunk_2077 "Cyberpunk 2077")*'s four nominations—twice as many as its original nominations in [2021](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2021 "The Game Awards 2021")—particularly due to the game's [troubled launch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cyberpunk_2077#Technical_issues "Cyberpunk 2077").[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Den_of_Geek_Snubs-49)[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-TheGamer_Cyberpunk-50) Many considered *[Destiny 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Destiny_2 "Destiny 2")*'s Best Community Support nomination poorly timed, coming weeks after layoffs at developer [Bungie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bungie "Bungie"), including much of its community team.[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Game_Rant_Bungie-51)[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-VG247_Bungie-52)[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-GamesRadar_Bungie-53) Journalists felt several performances were overlooked and suggested Best Performance be split to consider leading and supporting performances to widen its scope.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Inverse_Snubs-54)[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-TheGamer_Performance-55)[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-TheGamer_Performances-56) *TheGamer*'s Stacey Henley found *[Pizza Tower](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pizza_Tower "Pizza Tower")*'s nomination for Best Debut Indie Game but not Best Independent Game incongruous.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-TheGamer_Indie-57)

The absence of nominations for *[Chained Echoes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chained_Echoes "Chained Echoes")* was highlighted as a flaw in the eligibility period for games released the preceding December;[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Game_Rant_Snub-58)[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Kotaku_Snubs-59) some writers opined the show had a [recency bias](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Recency_bias "Recency bias"), with half the Game of the Year nominees released in October.[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Inverse_Snubs-54)[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-TheGamer_Starfield-60) Many reporters and players highlighted the sole nomination for *[Starfield](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Starfield_(video_game) "Starfield (video game)")*, a [blockbuster](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blockbuster_(entertainment) "Blockbuster (entertainment)") game from a reputable developer,[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-BBC_Nominees-32)[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Den_of_Geek_Snubs-49)[[52]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Eurogamer_Starfield-61) though some found it appropriate due to the game's lesser quality compared to its competition.[[51]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-TheGamer_Starfield-60)[[53]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-PC_Gamer_Starfield-62) The lack of nominations for *[Hogwarts Legacy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hogwarts_Legacy "Hogwarts Legacy")* was similarly highlighted, with some citing [the game's divisiveness](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hogwarts_Legacy#controversy "Hogwarts Legacy") as a possible reason,[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Den_of_Geek_Snubs-49)[[54]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Game_Rant_Hogwarts-63) though others felt it was due to its relative quality.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Kotaku_Snubs-59)[[55]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-TheGamer_Hogwarts-64)[[56]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Escapist_Hogwarts-65) Some lamented the omission of *[Octopath Traveler 2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Octopath_Traveler_2 "Octopath Traveler 2")*,[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Den_of_Geek_Snubs-49)[[57]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Mary_Sue_Snub-66)[[58]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Game_Rant_Snubs-67) and others felt *[Final Fantasy XVI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Final_Fantasy_XVI "Final Fantasy XVI")* was snubbed a [Game of the Year](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Award_for_Game_of_the_Year "The Game Award for Game of the Year") nomination.[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Kotaku_Snubs-59)[[59]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-TheGamer_Nominees-68)

Several journalists and viewers expressed confusion at *[Dave the Diver](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dave_the_Diver "Dave the Diver")*'s Best Independent Game nomination as its developer, Mintrocket, is a subsidiary of the larger company [Nexon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nexon "Nexon"), which previously claimed the game was "not necessarily" an [indie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indie_game "Indie game");[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Inverse_Snubs-54)[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-TheGamer_Indie-57) *TheGamer*'s Henley wrote that *Baldur's Gate 3* was "technically an entirely independent game" but was likely not considered eligible due to developer Larian Studios's employee count and use of an existing intellectual property.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-TheGamer_Indie-57) In response, Keighley said "independent can mean different things to different people" and opted to allow the jury to decide the final selections.[[60]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-VGC_Indie-69) *TheGamer*'s Jade King called Games for Impact "a locker to stuff all the diverse games into", with four of its six nominees not receiving any other nominations, and felt it was typically limited to independent games despite others fitting the criteria.[[61]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-TheGamer_Impact-70)

### Ceremony

Before the ceremony, more than 3,000 game industry members, including 79 previous Future Class recipients[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Paste_Gaza-71)—more than half of the 150 members to date[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Eurogamer_Review-72)—signed an open letter calling for a statement to be read during the show addressing the ongoing [Gaza humanitarian crisis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gaza_humanitarian_crisis "Gaza humanitarian crisis"), supporting the rights of [Palestinians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palestinians "Palestinians") and calling for a [ceasefire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ceasefire "Ceasefire"), and asking the industry to address the dehumanization of people from [South West Asia and North Africa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_West_Asia_and_North_Africa "South West Asia and North Africa") and their portrayal as villains or terrorists in games. The letter's author, 2021 Future Class recipient Younès Rabii, said it was motivated by [Meg Jayanth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meg_Jayanth "Meg Jayanth")'s withdrawal as a presenter at the [Golden Joystick Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Joystick_Awards "Golden Joystick Awards") in October after being barred from making a statement about Palestinians.[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Axios_Gaza-73)[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Polygon_Gaza-74)[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-PC_Gamer_Gaza-75) *[The Mary Sue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Mary_Sue "The Mary Sue")*'s Ana Valens bemoaned the show's lack of response[[67]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Mary_Sue_Gaza-76) and *[Paste](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paste_(magazine) "Paste (magazine)")*'s Garrett Martin criticized it as "cowardly".[[62]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Paste_Gaza-71) *[Rock Paper Shotgun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rock_Paper_Shotgun "Rock Paper Shotgun")*'s Alice Bell felt the show only would have voiced support if it "was a profitable stance rather than a moral one".[[68]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-RPS_Review-77) After the ceremony, developers of nominees *[Goodbye Volcano High](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goodbye_Volcano_High "Goodbye Volcano High")* and *[Venba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Venba_(video_game) "Venba (video game)")* said they had planned to acknowledge the crisis in their acceptance speeches.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-IGN_Review-1) Keighley spoke with Future Class members after the show; some members felt he was deflective and unprepared, while others found the meeting productive and hopeful.[[69]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Wired_Gaza-78)[[70]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Game_Developer_Gaza-79) Members gave a presentation to Keighley and Bouchac in December about their negative experiences at the show and lack of resources and opportunities throughout the year; some felt their complaints were taken seriously and that the program consequently improved.[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Game_Awards_2023#cite_note-Game_Developer_Future_Class-12)
